text.en: A pencil in water looks bent. Light changes direction when it goes from one medium to another. This is refraction, and lenses use it.

Refraction is the change of direction of light when it enters a different medium, because its speed changes.
Going from air to glass, light bends towards the normal; going from glass to air, it bends away from the normal.
Snell's law: sin i / sin r is constant for the pair of media, and this constant is the refractive index.
The refractive index of a medium is n = speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in the medium. A higher index means a denser optical medium.
A convex lens converges light and a concave lens diverges it.
Lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, and magnification m = v/u. A convex lens can form real and virtual images; a concave lens only forms virtual, erect, diminished images.
Power of a lens P = 1/f with f in metres; the unit is dioptre (D). A convex lens has positive power and a concave lens has negative power.
Lenses used together have the sum of their powers: P = P1 + P2.

problem.en: An object is 20 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the image position.

text.en: v = +20 cm, so the image is real and on the other side.
m = v/u = -1, so the image is inverted and the same size.

prompt.en: What are refraction, refractive index and lens power?

points.en: Refractive index n = c/v; Snell's law sin i / sin r = n.
Convex lens positive power; concave lens negative power.
